To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the top 50 food sources of calories, protein, and carbohydrate provide 75% of the total population intake; 2) the top 20 food sources of total fat, saturated fatty acids, linoleic acids, and cholesterol provide 75% to 80% of the total nutrient intake; and 3) the top 10 food sources of oleic acids provide 70% of the total intake.
the major sources of energy, protein, and fat in the American diet are breads, cereals, and meats, with dairy products and fats and sweets contributing lesser amounts.
the top 50 food contributors of calories, protein, carbohydrates, total fat, and saturated fat are similar for the total population and the subgroups defined by gender, age, or ethnicity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method of dietary assessment that is both valid and practical.
the development of a method for assessing dietary adequacy which can be used by the general public and health care professionals.
the use of food frequency questionnaires (FFQs) as a means to measure the dietary intake of individuals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the American diet is a complex one, and that it is not possible to make a simple statement about the nutrient content of the average American diet.
there is a need for a more complete understanding of the relationship between dietary patterns and disease.
the major sources of energy and nutrients in the U.S. diet are the following: for calories, fats and sugars, for protein, meat and dairy products, and for carbohydrates, grains and potatoes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the American diet is high in total fat and cholesterol, but low in oleic acid and linoleic acid.
, in the American diet, 10% of the total calories come from protein; 47% from carbohydrate; 43% from total fat; 13% from saturated fat; and less than 1% from cholesterol.
, in the U.S. population as a whole, the top contributors to nutrient intake are not necessarily the foods that would be considered the most healthful.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in general, there is little variation among the top contributors of each of the nutrients examined.
the top 50 sources of calories, protein, carbohydrates, total fat, and saturated fat account for 75% or more of the total intake of these nutrients.
there are many different ways to eat a healthy diet.
